children: Asia high-yield credit continues to be a compelling opportunity in the region, says John Li at J.P. Morgan Private Bank. After a record default wave, Li says the asset class has turned a corner. Total 1H returns are approaching 4% and defaults are close to zero year-to-date. Yields remain attractive, while stronger corporate balance sheets and a more supportive refinancing backdrop should help keep defaults contained. Asia HY could also benefit from renewed investor interest in emerging-market debt. Asia credit as a whole enters 2H on solid footing after outperforming broader fixed-income markets in 1H, with carry likely to be the dominant driver of returns in a higher-for-longer rates environment. "Over the next 12 months, we expect total returns of approximately 5.0%-5.5% for Asia IG and 7%-8% for Asia HY." (fabiana.negrinochoa@wsj.com)
